The test image shows a **stem** with a gray-brown dusty/fuzzy coating - classic fungal sporulation on a tomato stem. The gray powdery/velvety growth on the stem surface is the key feature. Yellowing foliage visible in background.

Top candidates: **Gray_Mold** (gray-brown spore mass on stems), **Powdery_Mildew** (white powdery coating), **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cottony mycelium on stem).

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
That's a microscope view. Let me check the other Gray Mold stem reference and also Powdery Mildew.
Gray Mold Bugwood_23 shows brown necrotic lesion with gray sporulation on stem - very similar to the test image. Let me check two more candidates.
Powdery Mildew shows white powder on leaves - different from the gray-brown stem coating in the test. Let me check Sclerotinia.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Stem with elongated gray-brown dusty/velvety coating, yellowing foliage in background
- **Gray_Mold stem ref (Bugwood_23)**: Brown necrotic lesion at stem node with gray sporulation and yellowing leaf - very close match
- **Powdery_Mildew ref**: White powder on leaves - different location and color, ruled out
- **Sclerotinia ref**: Bleached white stem with embedded black sclerotia near soil line - distinct appearance, ruled out

The gray-brown velvety sporulation along the tomato stem in the test image is characteristic of **Botrytis gray mold**. The KB description matches: "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass on infected tissue; stem lesions may expand to girdle the entire stem."
